question: Will Rodrigo Duterte’s trial at the ICC open before December 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Trial Chamber III set 30 Nov 2026 for the opening back on 27 May. The 8 Oct 2026 decision found Duterte fit, with adaptive sitting hours and continuous medical monitoring. The 13 Oct status conference planned the daily schedule around 30 Nov, with an evidentiary block in December. I found no pending request to postpone, and earlier fitness appeals were refused. The main risks: an acute health event (he is 81 and frail), late disclosure fights, or any slip of even one day (to 1 Dec or later), which resolves NO because there is only a one-day margin. Reference class: ICC trial openings about 6 weeks before their scheduled date, with fitness settled; most go ahead, but some slipped (Yekatom, Said, Abd-Al-Rahman). No human prediction market found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold.
calls.dossier:
- 27 May 2026 (Rappler/Inquirer/ICC press via GlobalSecurity): At its 1st status conference, Trial Chamber III set the opening of Prosecutor v. Duterte for 30 Nov 2026.
- 8 Oct 2026 (ICC press release; kohenavocats summary): The Chamber unanimously found Duterte fit to stand trial, based on an independent expert panel. Adaptive measures: sitting hours set case by case, continuous monitoring by the ICC Medical Officer, immediate reporting of health changes. Fitness is treated as a continuing condition the Chamber can revisit.
- 13 Oct 2026 (Inquirer/Philstar): The 4th status conference covered the daily sitting schedule, opening statements and a first evidentiary block in December 2026. Prosecution's estimated time cut from 193 to 173 hours. Defense asked for a 10,000-item cap on disclosure; the presiding judge (Korner) warned it could violate disclosure obligations. No written decision yet.
- 17 Oct 2026 (Philstar/Tribune): Prosecution filed Rule 68 requests to use prior recorded testimony of 5 witnesses.
- Feb 2026 (GMA/Inquirer): The ICC refused Duterte's leave to appeal the pre-trial fitness ruling. Proceedings had already been postponed about 5 months earlier, when the confirmation hearing was delayed over fitness in 2025.
- Malaya (date unclear, could not open): Duterte's new lawyer urged postponing the trial start until his fitness is assured.
- 19 Oct 2026 (CDN): Media still report 30 Nov as the start date.
- Status quo: the opening goes ahead on 30 Nov 2026.
- Base rate: some ICC trial openings slipped by weeks to months (Yekatom/Ngaissona 2020 to 2021, Abd-Al-Rahman Feb to Apr 2022, Said several times), but most slips were ordered well before the final 6 weeks. No systematic count found.
- Resolves off the ICC case page or credible reports of the formal opening, not off scheduling announcements.
- Event window: now -> before 1 Dec 2026. The scheduled date leaves a one-day margin, so any slip of a day or more means NO. As of 19 Oct, about 6 weeks remain.
- Searched but not found: any pending defense postponement motion filed after 8 Oct; any prediction market on this event.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the factual record: the 30 Nov opening was set 27 May and kept at the 13 Oct status conference; the fitness decision is dated 28 Sep and was announced 8 Oct; no postponement motion has been found; no prediction market exists. The spread (0.81-0.86) is purely judgment about the residual slip risk with a one-day margin. I had no web access and could not check anything new. Judgment: late (<6 weeks) ICC postponements are uncommon, and this chamber has firmly rejected delay bids. However, the accused's age and frailty, fitness being a 'continuing condition', and the zero-margin date leave ~15-17% risk. I land at 0.84.
